extracted.intended_audience: handlers, dairy associations, milk producers, and other stakeholders participating in milk marketing order rulemaking; regulatory commenters
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and proposed regulatory text for amending the Inland Empire milk marketing order (definitions, pooling qualifications, diversion limits, classification/pricing) together with related Federal regulatory directives appearing in the same Federal Register pages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plant definition (exclude reload facility)
rubrics_metrics.description: The plant definition should be revised to exclude a reload facility: an establishment used only for transferring bulk milk from one tank truck to another shall not be a plant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale and examples: A reload point is primarily a facility at which milk is pumped from one tanker into another for delivery and has no storage or cooling facilities; it involves comparatively small investment and allowing reloads to qualify as plants enables exploitation of pooling provisions, increases diversion and undermines orderly marketing. No testimony opposed the exclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pool distributing plant qualification standard
rubrics_metrics.description: A distributing plant qualifies for pooling if the lesser of 250,000 pounds or 20 percent of its Grade A milk receipts is distributed on routes in the marketing area during a month.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposal to change the in-area route distribution standard to the lesser of 100,000 pounds or 10 percent was considered but denied: record evidence did not show nonpool plants were causing disorderly marketing; current requirements deemed adequate and integrity of classification/pricing safeguarded by payment options for partially regulated distributing plants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pool supply plant qualifying percentages and months
rubrics_metrics.description: A supply pool plant is a plant from which 50 percent or more of the skim milk and butterfat in its dairy farm supply of Grade A milk is forwarded to pool distributing plants during the current month in the period of September through November, or 20 percent or more during December through August.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retention/withdrawal rule: Any plant that forwarded more than 50 percent for the entire September-November period remains a pool plant for the following December–August unless the operator files a written request with the market administrator prior to the first day of any month to withdraw. Rationale: shift in seasonal production warrants moving qualifying period from October–December to September–November.

rubrics_metrics.name: Producer milk diversion percentages — cooperative associations
rubrics_metrics.description: A cooperative association may divert for its account milk of any member producer eligible for diversion, but total diverted quantity may not exceed 50 percent in April–August, 30 percent in December–March, and 20 percent in September–November of its total member milk received at all pool plants or diverted therefrom during the month.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two or more cooperative associations may have allowable diversions computed on the basis of combined deliveries of their member producers if each association files a written request with the market administrator. Rationale: increased production and movements to nonpool plants made present diversion allowances inadequate in all months; no opposition testimony to increasing percentages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Producer milk diversion percentages — handlers operating pool plants
rubrics_metrics.description: A handler operating a pool plant may divert for his account milk of any producer eligible for diversion (other than members of cooperative associations diverting under the coop rule), but total diverted quantity may not exceed 50 percent in April–August, 30 percent in December–March, and 20 percent in September–November of the milk received at or diverted from such pool plant during the month from such producers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parallels cooperative diversion limits; ensures seasonal variation and places monthly caps on diversions by handlers; reflects the same rationale about production increases and need for higher allowable diversion during certain months.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seasonal variation in diversion allowances (include August)
rubrics_metrics.description: The order should provide seasonal variation in the amount of milk which may be diverted; August is included in the period of maximum diversion (April–August) because production/need patterns now associate August with months of high diversion need.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Market data cited: diversion percentages in April–July and August in 1965–1966 substantiate including August in maximum diversion period; objective is to reflect varying need to divert milk during different months.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification and pricing — no change without evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: No amendment is provided concerning classification and pricing provisions because no testimony or record evidence showed disorderly marketing related to these provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy: absence of supporting evidence (testimony or data) in the hearing record justifies retaining existing classification and pricing provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Findings/conclusions must be based on hearing record and evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Findings and conclusions are based on evidence presented at the hearing and the record thereof; briefs and proposed findings submitted by interested parties are considered but will be denied to the extent inconsistent with the findings in the decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Official notice of market administrator statistical summaries was taken where appropriate. Requests to adopt suggested findings inconsistent with the decision are denied for reasons stated in the decision. This establishes that documentary evidence, testimony, and official notices form the basis for changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory text — §1133.7 revised plant definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Revised regulatory definition (§1133.7): 'Plant' means the land, buildings, facilities, and equipment... maintained primarily for receiving, processing or packaging of fluid milk and milk products. However, an establishment that is separate from the foregoing operating unit and used only for transferring bulk milk from one tank truck to another shall not be a plant under this definition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the prescriptive regulatory revision implementing the exclusion of reload points from the plant definition; it should be used verbatim in the order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory text — §1133.8(b) supply pool plant paragraph
rubrics_metrics.description: §1133.8(b) (as revised) prescribes that a 'supply pool plant' is any plant from which there is forwarded to a pool distributing plant(s) 50 percent or more each of the skim milk and butterfat in its dairy farm supply of Grade A milk during the current month in September–November, or 20 percent or more during December–August; plants forwarding >50% in the whole Sept–Nov period are pool plants for the following Dec–Aug unless operator files written withdrawal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This paragraph provides the precise numeric and procedural rules for automatic pooling status and the administrative mechanism for withdrawal of pool status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory text — §1133.12(c)(1) & (2) producer milk diversion rules
rubrics_metrics.description: §1133.12(c)(1): Cooperative associations may divert milk for their account subject to monthly caps (50% Apr–Aug, 30% Dec–Mar, 20% Sep–Nov) of total member milk received at pool plants or diverted. §1133.12(c)(2): Handlers operating pool plants may divert subject to same monthly caps of milk received at or diverted from such pool plant from producers not members of diversioning cooperatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also prescribes that two or more cooperatives may compute allowable diversions on combined deliveries if each files written request with the market administrator. Use these precise percentages and filing requirements in administrative enforcement and computations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shipping temperatures for specified biological products (§73.40)
rubrics_metrics.description: The following products shall be maintained during shipment at specified temperatures: Whole Blood (Human) 1–10°C; Packed Red Blood Cells (Human) 1–10°C; Poliovirus Vaccine(s) — temperature which will maintain ice continuously in a solid state; Single Donor Plasma (Human), Frozen — −18°C or colder; Smallpox Liquid Vaccine — a temperature which will maintain ice continuously in a solid state; Yellow Fever Vaccine — a temperature which will maintain ice continuously in a solid state.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This prescribes product-by-product shipping temperature requirements; use exact temperature specifications and the 'maintain ice continuously in a solid state' requirement where stated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manufacturing responsibilities for Packed Red Blood Cells (§73.327)
rubrics_metrics.description: Manufacturing responsibilities, periodic check on sterile technique and reissue shall be carried out in all respects for Packed Red Blood Cells (Human) as prescribed in Section 73.304 for Whole Blood (Human).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cross-reference: Packed Red Blood Cells must meet the same manufacturing and sterility checks/processes required for Whole Blood under §73.304.

rubrics_metrics.name: Airworthiness directive for Glasflugel H-301 gliders (Tost Type Universal 53 coupling)
rubrics_metrics.description: To reduce the release load when asymmetrical loads occur, install tow cable deflectors on each side of the Q hook in accordance with Glasflugel Modification No. 23 (Drawing No. 301-15-16) or later LBA-approved issue or equivalent approved by FAA Chief, Aircraft Certification Staff, Europe/Africa/Middle East Region.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicability: Glasflugel H-301 'Libelle' gliders, Serial Nos. 2 through 55, equipped with Tost Type Universal 53 couplings. Compliance required within the next 100 hours' time in service after the effective date of the AD unless already accomplished. Rationale: instances of failure to disengage properly under asymmetrical loads; prior modification (Tost Mod No.2/65) not appropriate for these serials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria considered in granting extensions to file comments (FCC practice)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission may extend time for filing comments/reply comments when good cause is shown due to practical difficulties such as holiday weekends reducing available time, need to review and analyze sizeable/detailed documents, and availability constraints of engineering consultants and legal counsel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission weighs petitioner reasons and public interest; extensions are granted under specified statutory/rule authorities (e.g., Communications Act sections cited and Commission rule sections). Use these factors when requesting extensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: AID redelegation limits and authority for investment guaranties and surveys
rubrics_metrics.description: Authority redelegated to named AID officials to authorize, issue, and amend investment guaranties under section 221 of the Foreign Assistance Act, with monetary and other limits: (a) Executive Director/Managing Director may authorize guaranties covering investments in form of royalties or not exceeding $5 million and make related approvals under sections 221(a),(b),(c) and 222(a); (b) Director, Insurance Division may authorize guaranties not exceeding $500,000 and participate up to $5,000 in financing surveys under section 231.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Delegations are conditional (consistent with law and specified Delegations Nos.), include authority to make statutory determinations, and contain restrictions on amendments that increase amounts or participation above stated ceilings. Use the exact monetary ceilings and section references when applying delegation.
